```{r}
#| label: setup
library(toxval)
has_drc <- requireNamespace("drc", quietly = TRUE)
# the columns read in the text; each result also has `metric`, `sig_val`,
# `type`, `anchor` and `asymptote`
show_nsec <- function(x) {
  x[, c(
    "direction", "estimate", "conf.low", "conf.high",
    "control", "reference", "ecnsec", "ecnsec.low", "ecnsec.high"
  )]
}
```

```{r}
#| label: formatting
#| echo: false
# wide enough for the nine columns `show_nsec()` prints
options(width = 100)
fmt <- function(x, digits = 3) {
  formatC(signif(x, digits), digits = digits, format = "fg", flag = "#")
}
# controls and references are stated to the step of the constructed controls
ctl <- function(x) sprintf("%.2f", x)
prop <- function(x) sprintf("%.3f", x)
pct <- function(x) paste(format(round(100 * x, 1), nsmall = 1), "per cent")
# inline values from the `drc` fit are evaluated only when `drc` is installed,
# so the vignette still builds without it
if_drc <- function(expr) if (has_drc) expr else "(not computed: drc is not installed)"
probs <- c(0.5, 0.025, 0.975)
```

## Background

The no-significant-effect concentration (NSEC) is the lowest concentration at
which the fitted response differs from the control response by more than the
uncertainty in the control allows. `nsec()` computes it from realisations of the
fitted curve. A realisation is one posterior draw of a Bayesian fit, or one
parametric bootstrap replicate of a frequentist fit, evaluated over a grid of
concentrations. `toxval_predict()` builds that grid and those realisations, and
stores them in a `toxval_pred` object.

For each curve, `nsec()` does three things.

1. It sets one reference response for each direction. The decreasing reference
   is the `sig_val` quantile of the control realisations, and the increasing
   reference is the `1 - sig_val` quantile. The control realisation is a
   realisation's predicted response at the control concentration, by default
   the lowest concentration in the data, where the grid starts. `sig_val`
   defaults to 0.01.
2. It finds, for each realisation, the first concentration at which that
   realisation crosses the reference in each direction. Between grid points the
   crossing is found by linear interpolation.
3. It summarises the crossings by the quantiles in `prob_vals`, by default the
   median and the 2.5 and 97.5 per cent quantiles.

Both directions are sought on every call, and each is returned as a row with a
`direction` column. A direction in which no realisation crosses is returned with
`NA` estimates. The NSEC reference is one value per curve, shared by every
realisation. The ECx reference differs on this point: it is computed for each
realisation from that realisation's own control, as
`vignette("ecx-definition", package = "toxval")` describes.

## Constructed realisations

The examples are built by hand with `new_toxval_pred()`, so that every value
`nsec()` returns can be computed independently. Each set has 101 realisations
whose controls are evenly spaced. These values are constructed, not sampled from
a fit.

`nsec()` takes the reference with R's default quantile method (type 7). For 101
values the quantile at probability $p$ is the value at position $1 + 100p$ in
sorted order, interpolated where that position is not a whole number. The 0.01
quantile is therefore the second-smallest control, and the 0.99 quantile the
hundredth. The crossings are summarised by the same method unless a realisation
in that row is censored, as described under
[Realisations with no crossing](#realisations-with-no-crossing).

The helper below evaluates one curve shape at each control and stores the
result. The `meta` list follows the slot contract documented in
`?new_toxval_pred`. `family = "beta"` marks a response on the proportion scale,
and `x_control` is the control concentration, 0 here, which is also the first
grid value.

```{r}
#| label: build-pred
build_pred <- function(shape, controls, x_vec, family = "gaussian", ...) {
  curves <- t(vapply(
    controls,
    function(control) shape(control, x_vec),
    numeric(length(x_vec))
  ))
  new_toxval_pred(
    curves = list(curves),
    keys = data.frame(row.names = 1L),
    x_vec = x_vec,
    meta = list(
      source_class = "constructed",
      x_var = "x",
      group_var = NULL,
      multi_var = NULL,
      resolution = length(x_vec),
      x_range = range(x_vec),
      x_control = 0,
      family = family,
      realisation = "draws",
      n_realisation = length(controls),
      seed = NULL,
      ...
    )
  )
}
```

```{r}
#| label: plot-helper
#| echo: false
# Grey lines are every tenth realisation; dashed lines the references;
# solid and dotted vertical lines the NSEC estimate and its interval, in the
# colour of the direction.
direction_col <- c(decreasing = "#2a78d6", increasing = "#eb6834")
plot_nsec <- function(pred, result, ylab = "Response", every = 10) {
  x <- pred$x_vec
  curves <- pred$curves[[1]]
  shown <- seq(1, nrow(curves), by = every)
  # room above the highest reference for its label
  y_lim <- range(curves[shown, ], result$reference)
  y_lim[2] <- y_lim[2] + 0.08 * diff(y_lim)
  old_par <- graphics::par(mar = c(4, 4, 1, 1))
  on.exit(graphics::par(old_par))
  graphics::matplot(
    x,
    t(curves[shown, , drop = FALSE]),
    type = "l",
    lty = 1,
    col = "grey75",
    ylim = y_lim,
    xlab = "Concentration",
    ylab = ylab,
    las = 1,
    bty = "l"
  )
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(result))) {
    d <- result$direction[i]
    graphics::abline(h = result$reference[i], col = direction_col[[d]], lty = 2, lwd = 2)
    graphics::text(
      max(x),
      result$reference[i],
      paste(d, "reference"),
      adj = c(1, -0.4),
      col = "grey20",
      cex = 0.8
    )
    if (!is.na(result$estimate[i])) {
      graphics::abline(v = result$estimate[i], col = direction_col[[d]], lwd = 2)
      graphics::abline(
        v = c(result$conf.low[i], result$conf.high[i]),
        col = direction_col[[d]],
        lty = 3,
        lwd = 1.5
      )
    }
  }
}
```

## A decreasing response

The first set has controls from 9.00 to 11.00 in steps of 0.02. Every
realisation declines exponentially from its control, $y = c\,e^{-x/5}$, over a
grid of 500 concentrations from 0 to 10.

```{r}
#| label: decreasing
controls <- seq(9, 11, by = 0.02)
decline <- function(control, x) control * exp(-x / 5)
dec_pred <- build_pred(decline, controls, seq(0, 10, length.out = 500))
dec <- nsec(dec_pred)
print(dec, width = Inf)
```

```{r}
#| label: decreasing-check
#| echo: false
grid_step <- function(pred) diff(pred$x_vec)[1]
r_dec <- controls[2]
r_inc <- controls[100]
# a realisation whose control is below the reference does not cross it and is
# placed at `x_control`, 0 here; one whose control equals the reference crosses
# at the first grid value, also 0
nsec_dec_hand <- ifelse(controls > r_dec, 5 * log(controls / r_dec), 0)
q_dec_hand <- quantile(nsec_dec_hand, probs, names = FALSE)
ecnsec_dec_hand <- quantile(1 - r_dec / controls, probs, names = FALSE)
median_control <- median(controls)
stopifnot(
  sum(controls < r_dec) == 1,
  which(controls < r_dec) == 1,
  max(controls) > r_inc,
  abs(dec$estimate[1] - 5 * log(median_control / r_dec)) < grid_step(dec_pred),
  isTRUE(all.equal(dec$reference, c(r_dec, r_inc))),
  all(abs(unlist(dec[1, c("estimate", "conf.low", "conf.high")]) - q_dec_hand) <
    grid_step(dec_pred)),
  isTRUE(all.equal(
    unlist(dec[1, c("ecnsec", "ecnsec.low", "ecnsec.high")]),
    ecnsec_dec_hand,
    check.attributes = FALSE
  )),
  all(is.na(dec$estimate[2]))
)
```

The decreasing reference is `r ctl(dec$reference[1])`, the second-smallest
control, and the increasing reference is `r ctl(dec$reference[2])`, the
hundredth. A realisation with control $c$ reaches the decreasing reference at
$x = 5 \log(c / `r ctl(r_dec)`)$. The median realisation has a control of
`r ctl(median_control)`, so its NSEC is
$5 \log(`r ctl(median_control)` / `r ctl(r_dec)`) = `r fmt(5 * log(median_control / r_dec))`$,
and `nsec()` reports `r fmt(dec$estimate[1])`. The interval is
`r fmt(dec$conf.low[1])` to `r fmt(dec$conf.high[1])`. It agrees to within one
grid step (`r fmt(grid_step(dec_pred))`) with the 2.5 and 97.5 per cent
quantiles of the `r length(controls)` crossings given by this formula, taking 0 for the
realisation with control `r ctl(controls[1])`. That realisation starts below the
decreasing reference, and is placed by the rule given under
[Realisations with no crossing](#realisations-with-no-crossing).

The increasing row has `NA` estimates because no realisation rises. Its
`reference` and `ecnsec` still describe the response level that was sought.

```{r}
#| label: fig-decreasing
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Every tenth realisation of the decreasing set, with both references and the decreasing NSEC and its interval."
plot_nsec(dec_pred, dec)
```

@fig-decreasing shows that the realisations differ only in their control, so
the spread of the NSEC comes entirely from the spread of the control. The
lowest curve shown, with control `r ctl(controls[1])`, starts below the
decreasing reference. The highest, with control `r ctl(max(controls))`, starts
above the increasing reference, and no curve rises towards it.

## The effect at the NSEC

`ecnsec` is the effect that the reference represents, expressed as a proportion
of the span named by `type`. It is the inverse of the ECx reference under the
same `type`: an ECx at proportion $p$ sets its reference $p$ of the span away
from the control, and `ecnsec` gives the $p$ at which that reference would equal
the NSEC reference. Under the default, `type = "absolute"`, the decreasing span
of a realisation is its control, so for a realisation with control $c$ and
reference $R$

$$
\text{ecnsec} = \frac{c - R}{c}.
$$

`ecnsec` is computed for each realisation and summarised by the same quantiles
as the NSEC. For the decreasing set its median is
$1 - `r ctl(r_dec)` / 10 = `r fmt(dec$ecnsec[1])`$: the decreasing reference
lies `r pct(dec$ecnsec[1])` below the median control. For the increasing row the
span is again the control, since this response is not a proportion, and the
reference lies `r pct(dec$ecnsec[2])` above the median control. The
`vignette("ecx-definition", package = "toxval")` gives the span for each `type`
and direction.

Calling `ecx()` at the median `ecnsec` tests the inverse relation.

```{r}
#| label: ecx-inverse
ecx(dec_pred, proportion = dec$ecnsec[1])
```

```{r}
#| label: ecx-inverse-check
#| echo: false
ecx_at_ecnsec <- ecx(dec_pred, proportion = dec$ecnsec[1])
stopifnot(
  abs(ecx_at_ecnsec$estimate[1] - dec$estimate[1]) < grid_step(dec_pred),
  # every realisation has the same shape, so the interval has zero width
  isTRUE(all.equal(ecx_at_ecnsec$conf.low[1], ecx_at_ecnsec$conf.high[1])),
  abs(ecx_at_ecnsec$estimate[1] + 5 * log(1 - dec$ecnsec[1])) < grid_step(dec_pred)
)
```

The decreasing ECx at proportion `r fmt(dec$ecnsec[1])` is
`r fmt(ecx_at_ecnsec$estimate[1])`, the NSEC of the median realisation. Its
interval has zero width because every realisation here has the same shape, so
each reaches a given proportion of its own control at the same concentration,
$-5 \log(1 - p)$.

`type` changes `ecnsec` but not the NSEC. Under `type = "range"` the decreasing
span is the control minus the lowest response of the realisation over the grid,
here $c\,(1 - e^{-2})$.

```{r}
#| label: ecnsec-range
dec_range <- nsec(dec_pred, type = "range")
show_nsec(dec_range)
```

```{r}
#| label: ecnsec-range-check
#| echo: false
stopifnot(
  identical(dec_range$estimate, dec$estimate),
  identical(dec_range$conf.low, dec$conf.low),
  identical(dec_range$conf.high, dec$conf.high),
  isTRUE(all.equal(dec_range$ecnsec[1], dec$ecnsec[1] / (1 - exp(-2)))),
  is.na(dec_range$ecnsec[2])
)
```

The NSEC and its interval are identical to those under `"absolute"`. The median
decreasing `ecnsec` is `r fmt(dec_range$ecnsec[1])`, which is
$`r fmt(dec$ecnsec[1])` / (1 - e^{-2})$. The increasing `ecnsec` is `NA` because
a declining curve has no response above its control, so its increasing span
under `"range"` is zero. `type = "relative"` measures to the asymptote of the
fitted equation, which a constructed `toxval_pred` supplies only through its
`asymptote` slot.

`nsec()` refuses `type = "direct"`.

```{r}
#| label: direct
#| error: true
nsec(dec_pred, type = "direct")
```

Under `"direct"` the ECx reference is a response value supplied by the user,
with no span. The `ecnsec` would then be the NSEC reference itself, the same in
every realisation, and the `reference` column already reports it. `ecx()` keeps
`type = "direct"`, where the supplied value sets the reference and the ECx
varies between realisations.

## An increasing response

The second set is a proportion, such as mortality, that rises from its control
towards 1, $y = 1 - (1 - c)\,e^{-x/5}$. The controls run from 0.050 to 0.150 in
steps of 0.001, over the same grid. `family = "beta"` records that the response
is a proportion.

```{r}
#| label: increasing
inc_controls <- seq(0.05, 0.15, by = 0.001)
rise <- function(control, x) 1 - (1 - control) * exp(-x / 5)
inc_pred <- build_pred(
  rise,
  inc_controls,
  seq(0, 10, length.out = 500),
  family = "beta"
)
inc <- nsec(inc_pred)
show_nsec(inc)
```

```{r}
#| label: increasing-check
#| echo: false
r_up <- inc_controls[100]
median_inc <- median(inc_controls)
nsec_inc_hand <- ifelse(
  inc_controls < r_up,
  5 * log((1 - inc_controls) / (1 - r_up)),
  0
)
q_inc_hand <- quantile(nsec_inc_hand, probs, names = FALSE)
ecnsec_inc_hand <- quantile(
  (r_up - inc_controls) / (1 - inc_controls),
  probs,
  names = FALSE
)
stopifnot(
  isTRUE(all.equal(inc$reference, inc_controls[c(2, 100)])),
  abs(inc$estimate[2] - 5 * log((1 - median_inc) / (1 - r_up))) <
    grid_step(inc_pred),
  isTRUE(all.equal(inc$ecnsec[2], (r_up - median_inc) / (1 - median_inc))),
  all(abs(unlist(inc[2, c("estimate", "conf.low", "conf.high")]) - q_inc_hand) <
    grid_step(inc_pred)),
  isTRUE(all.equal(
    unlist(inc[2, c("ecnsec", "ecnsec.low", "ecnsec.high")]),
    ecnsec_inc_hand,
    check.attributes = FALSE
  )),
  is.na(inc$estimate[1])
)
```

The increasing reference is the 0.99 quantile of the controls,
`r prop(inc$reference[2])`, the hundredth value. A realisation with control $c$
reaches it at $x = 5 \log\{(1 - c) / (1 - `r prop(r_up)`)\}$, which for the median
control of `r prop(median_inc)` is
`r fmt(5 * log((1 - median_inc) / (1 - r_up)))`. `nsec()` reports
`r fmt(inc$estimate[2])` (`r fmt(inc$conf.low[2])` to `r fmt(inc$conf.high[2])`),
in agreement with the formula to within one grid step. The decreasing row is
`NA`, since no realisation falls.

For a proportion the increasing span under `"absolute"` is $1 - c$, the distance
from the control to the upper bound of the response, so

$$
\text{ecnsec} = \frac{R - c}{1 - c},
$$

which is the extra risk at the NSEC. Its median is
$(`r prop(r_up)` - `r prop(median_inc)`) / (1 - `r prop(median_inc)`) = `r fmt(inc$ecnsec[2])`$. For a response that is
not a proportion the increasing span is the control itself, as in the
decreasing set.

## Realisations with no crossing

A realisation that never crosses the reference in the direction sought, within
the grid, has no NSEC of its own. `nsec()` treats it in one of four ways.

- A realisation whose control already lies at or beyond the reference, in the
  direction sought, is given `x_control`, the control concentration: by
  default the lowest concentration in the data the model was fitted to.
- The exception is such a realisation that shows no effect in the tested
  range. Its response first changes away from the effect as concentration
  rises from the control: it rises, for a decreasing NSEC, or falls, for an
  increasing one. It then passes to the no-effect side of the reference, above
  it for a decreasing NSEC and below it for an increasing one, and does not
  return. It is censored, as below. Changes smaller
  than `1e-8` times the realisation's largest absolute response are ignored in
  finding the first change, so a curve that is flat at the control is judged
  by the direction of its first larger change.
- A realisation that does not reach the reference within the grid is given
  `Inf`, which ranks it above every crossing. A quantile that falls among such
  realisations is reported as the highest concentration, and the call warns
  with the fraction of realisations that are censored.
- A realisation with no finite control, such as a bootstrap replicate outside
  the parameter space of the model, is excluded from the summary and counted
  in the warning.

Censoring follows from what a missing crossing means. A realisation that has not
reached the reference by the highest concentration would reach it, if at all, at
a higher one, so it belongs in the upper tail. Dropping it would report a
quantile of the realisations that crossed, which lies below the same quantile of
all of them. A realisation that starts past the reference and then passes to the
no-effect side is past it only because its own control lies in the tail of the
control realisations. Within the tested range it never departs from the control
towards the effect, so it is censored in the same way.

A censored realisation has a rank but no value, so a row that contains one is
summarised by observed order statistics, `quantile()` type 1, rather than by
type 7. Type 7 interpolates between adjacent sorted values. An interpolation
between the last crossing and a censored realisation has no finite value, so
under type 7 a quantile only partly among the censored realisations would be
reported as the highest concentration. Under type 1 the quantile at probability
$p$ of $n$ values is the value at position $\lceil np \rceil$ in sorted order.
The two types agree where the type 7 position, $1 + (n - 1)p$, is a whole
number, as it is for the median of 101 values. Elsewhere the switch changes the
quantile, including one well below the censored realisations, by at most the
gap between the two sorted values that type 7 interpolates between.

About a fraction `sig_val` of the realisations have a control at or beyond the
reference, by construction of the reference. In the decreasing set there is
one, whose control of `r ctl(controls[1])` lies below the reference of
`r ctl(r_dec)`. Its response falls, towards the effect, so it is placed at
`x_control`. With `sig_val = 0.05` more than 2.5 per cent of the realisations
are placed there, so they set the lower limit of the interval.

```{r}
#| label: sig-val
dec_05 <- nsec(dec_pred, sig_val = 0.05)
show_nsec(dec_05)
```

```{r}
#| label: sig-val-check
#| echo: false
n_below_05 <- sum(controls < dec_05$reference[1])
stopifnot(
  isTRUE(all.equal(dec_05$reference[1], controls[6])),
  n_below_05 / length(controls) > 0.025,
  dec_05$conf.low[1] == dec_pred$meta$x_control
)
```

The decreasing reference is now `r ctl(dec_05$reference[1])`, the sixth control.
The `r n_below_05` realisations with lower controls lie below it from the start.
They decline, as every realisation of this set does, so they are placed at
`x_control`, and the lower limit is `r fmt(dec_05$conf.low[1])`.

Those realisations are censored instead if they show no effect. The next set
keeps the controls and the declining curves of the decreasing set, except that
the `r n_below_05` realisations with controls below `r ctl(controls[6])` rise
slowly, $y = c\,e^{x/100}$.

```{r}
#| label: no-effect
rise_slowly <- function(control, x) control * exp(x / 100)
mixed_shape <- function(control, x) {
  if (control < controls[6]) rise_slowly(control, x) else decline(control, x)
}
mixed_pred <- build_pred(mixed_shape, controls, seq(0, 10, length.out = 500))
mixed <- nsec(mixed_pred, sig_val = 0.05, draws = TRUE)
show_nsec(mixed)
head(mixed$draws[[1]], 7)
```

```{r}
#| label: no-effect-check
#| echo: false
n_rise <- sum(controls < controls[6])
r_05 <- dec_05$reference[1]
# each rising realisation passes above the reference at 100 log(r / c)
rise_cross <- 100 * log(r_05 / controls[seq_len(n_rise)])
nsec_mixed_hand <- c(rep(Inf, n_rise), 5 * log(controls[-seq_len(n_rise)] / r_05))
q_mixed_hand <- quantile(nsec_mixed_hand, probs, names = FALSE, type = 1)
q_mixed_hand[is.infinite(q_mixed_hand)] <- max(mixed_pred$x_vec)
draws_mixed <- mixed$draws[[1]]$value.draw
stopifnot(
  n_rise == n_below_05,
  isTRUE(all.equal(mixed$reference[1], r_05)),
  # the rising realisations stay below the increasing reference
  rise_slowly(controls[n_rise], 10) < mixed$reference[2],
  all(is.infinite(draws_mixed[seq_len(n_rise)])),
  all(is.finite(draws_mixed[-seq_len(n_rise)])),
  all(abs(unlist(mixed[1, c("estimate", "conf.low", "conf.high")]) - q_mixed_hand) <
    grid_step(mixed_pred)),
  mixed$conf.high[1] == max(mixed_pred$x_vec),
  mixed$conf.low[1] > dec_05$conf.low[1],
  mixed$estimate[1] > dec_05$estimate[1],
  n_rise / length(controls) > 0.025
)
```

The reference is still `r ctl(mixed$reference[1])`, since the controls are
unchanged. Each of the `r n_rise` rising realisations passes above it by
$x = `r fmt(max(rise_cross))`$ and stays above it to the end of the grid. Its
response first changes away from a decreasing effect, and it then lies on the
no-effect side, so it shows no effect in the tested range. `nsec()` censors
it, and it is `Inf` in the `draws` column. Ranked above every crossing, the
censored realisations raise the lower limit from
`r fmt(dec_05$conf.low[1])` to `r fmt(mixed$conf.low[1])` and the median from
`r fmt(dec_05$estimate[1])` to `r fmt(mixed$estimate[1])`. They are
`r pct(n_rise / length(controls))` of the realisations, so the 97.5 per cent quantile
falls among them. It is reported as the highest concentration,
`r fmt(mixed$conf.high[1])`, and the call warns. A wider range would not remove
the censoring, since the response of these realisations rises further above the
reference as concentration increases. Each value agrees to within one grid step
with the order statistics of the crossings $5 \log(c / `r ctl(r_05)`)$ of the
declining realisations, with the rising ones ranked above them.

The decreasing set was also evaluated over a shorter grid, from 0 to 0.9. The
realisations with the highest controls decline too little in that range to
reach the reference, so they are censored. For a fitted model the range is set
with `x_range`. For a constructed `toxval_pred` it is the grid supplied, and
`nsec()` refuses `x_range`.

```{r}
#| label: censored
short_pred <- build_pred(decline, controls, seq(0, 0.9, length.out = 500))
short <- nsec(short_pred, draws = TRUE)
show_nsec(short)
tail(short$draws[[1]], 3)
```

```{r}
#| label: censored-check
#| echo: false
# the last grid point starts no interval, so a crossing at or beyond it is not
# found within the grid
n_censored <- sum(nsec_dec_hand >= max(short_pred$x_vec))
draws_short <- short$draws[[1]]$value.draw
n_real <- length(controls)
short_hand <- ifelse(nsec_dec_hand >= max(short_pred$x_vec), Inf, nsec_dec_hand)
q_short_hand <- quantile(short_hand, probs, names = FALSE, type = 1)
stopifnot(
  sum(is.infinite(draws_short)) == n_censored,
  # the censored realisations are those with the highest controls
  all(is.infinite(draws_short) == (seq_len(n_real) > n_real - n_censored)),
  n_censored / length(controls) > 0.025,
  short$conf.high[1] == max(short_pred$x_vec),
  is.infinite(q_short_hand[3]),
  all(abs(unlist(short[1, c("estimate", "conf.low")]) - q_short_hand[1:2]) <
    grid_step(short_pred)),
  # the lower limit is the third crossing, and the median the 51st
  short$conf.low[1] == sort(draws_short)[3],
  short$estimate[1] == sort(draws_short)[51],
  abs(short$estimate[1] - dec$estimate[1]) < grid_step(dec_pred),
  short$conf.low[1] < dec$conf.low[1]
)
```

`r n_censored` of the `r n_real` realisations, those with controls from
`r ctl(controls[n_real - n_censored + 1])` to `r ctl(max(controls))`, would
reach the reference beyond `r fmt(max(short_pred$x_vec))`. They are `Inf` in the
`draws` column, and are `r pct(n_censored / n_real)` of the realisations. The 97.5 per
cent quantile has 2.5 per cent of the realisations above it, so it falls among
the censored ones. It is reported as `r fmt(short$conf.high[1])`, the highest
concentration, and the call warns. The median, `r fmt(short$estimate[1])`, is
that of the full grid. The lower limit is `r fmt(short$conf.low[1])`, against
`r fmt(dec$conf.low[1])` on the full grid, although the realisations that set it
crossed within both ranges. With censored realisations in the row, the lower
limit is the third crossing. The full grid takes the value halfway between the
third and the fourth.

The upper limit should then be read as "at least `r fmt(short$conf.high[1])`":
the tested range did not extend far enough to bound it. Where the censored
realisations are fewer than 2.5 per cent, the upper limit lies below all of
them, and there is no warning.

```{r}
#| label: censored-few
few_pred <- build_pred(decline, controls, seq(0, 0.98, length.out = 500))
few <- nsec(few_pred, draws = TRUE)
show_nsec(few)
```

```{r}
#| label: censored-few-check
#| echo: false
draws_few <- few$draws[[1]]$value.draw
n_few <- sum(is.infinite(draws_few))
few_hand <- ifelse(nsec_dec_hand >= max(few_pred$x_vec), Inf, nsec_dec_hand)
q_few_hand <- quantile(few_hand, probs, names = FALSE, type = 1)
stopifnot(
  n_few == sum(nsec_dec_hand >= max(few_pred$x_vec)),
  n_few / length(controls) < 0.025,
  all(abs(unlist(few[1, c("estimate", "conf.low", "conf.high")]) - q_few_hand) <
    grid_step(few_pred)),
  # the upper limit is the 99th crossing, below the censored realisations
  few$conf.high[1] == sort(draws_few)[99],
  is.finite(few$conf.high[1]),
  few$conf.high[1] > dec$conf.high[1]
)
```

On a grid to `r fmt(max(few_pred$x_vec))`, `r n_few` realisations are censored.
They lie above the 97.5 per cent quantile, so the upper limit is a crossing,
`r fmt(few$conf.high[1])`, and there is no warning. It is the 99th crossing.
The full grid gives `r fmt(dec$conf.high[1])`, halfway between the 98th and the
99th, because that row has no censored realisation.

## A hormetic response

The third set uses the controls of the decreasing set with a hormetic shape,
$y = c\,(1 + x/2)\,e^{-x/4}$, over a grid of 500 concentrations from 0 to 20.
Each realisation rises to $2e^{-1/2} = `r fmt(2 * exp(-0.5))`$ times its control
at $x = 2$ and then declines. The references are those of the decreasing set,
since the controls are the same.

```{r}
#| label: hormetic
hormesis <- function(control, x) control * (1 + x / 2) * exp(-x / 4)
horm_pred <- build_pred(hormesis, controls, seq(0, 20, length.out = 500))
horm <- nsec(horm_pred)
show_nsec(horm)
```

```{r}
#| label: hormetic-check
#| echo: false
peak <- 2 * exp(-0.5)
shape <- function(x) (1 + x / 2) * exp(-x / 4)
# the first downward crossing lies after the peak for every realisation,
# including those whose control starts below the reference
horm_dec_hand <- vapply(
  controls,
  function(control) {
    stats::uniroot(
      function(x) control * shape(x) - r_dec,
      c(2, 20),
      tol = 1e-10
    )$root
  },
  numeric(1)
)
horm_inc_hand <- vapply(
  controls,
  function(control) {
    if (control >= r_inc) {
      return(0)
    }
    if (control * peak <= r_inc) {
      return(Inf)
    }
    stats::uniroot(
      function(x) control * shape(x) - r_inc,
      c(0, 2),
      tol = 1e-10
    )$root
  },
  numeric(1)
)
q_horm_dec <- quantile(horm_dec_hand, probs, names = FALSE)
# the increasing row has censored realisations, so it takes order statistics
q_horm_inc <- quantile(horm_inc_hand, probs, names = FALSE, type = 1)
q_horm_inc[is.infinite(q_horm_inc)] <- max(horm_pred$x_vec)
n_horm_censored <- sum(is.infinite(horm_inc_hand))
# the realisations themselves, to read the value given to the first one; the
# censoring warning was already shown by the call above
horm_draws <- suppressWarnings(nsec(horm_pred, draws = TRUE))$draws
horm_first_dec <- horm_draws[[1]]$value.draw[1]
stopifnot(
  controls[1] < r_dec,
  abs(horm_first_dec - horm_dec_hand[1]) < grid_step(horm_pred),
  # the censored realisations are those with the lowest controls
  all(is.infinite(horm_inc_hand) == (seq_len(n_real) <= n_horm_censored)),
  all(is.infinite(horm_draws[[2]]$value.draw) == is.infinite(horm_inc_hand)),
  all(abs(unlist(horm[1, c("estimate", "conf.low", "conf.high")]) - q_horm_dec) <
    grid_step(horm_pred)),
  all(abs(unlist(horm[2, c("estimate", "conf.low", "conf.high")]) - q_horm_inc) <
    grid_step(horm_pred)),
  horm$conf.high[2] == max(horm_pred$x_vec),
  n_horm_censored / length(controls) > 0.025,
  horm_dec_hand[1] > 2
)
```

Both rows have estimates. The decreasing NSEC is `r fmt(horm$estimate[1])`
(`r fmt(horm$conf.low[1])` to `r fmt(horm$conf.high[1])`), where the declining
part of each curve falls through `r ctl(r_dec)`. The increasing NSEC is
`r fmt(horm$estimate[2])` (`r fmt(horm$conf.low[2])` to
`r fmt(horm$conf.high[2])`), where the rising part passes `r ctl(r_inc)`. Both
agree with crossings found by `uniroot()` to within one grid step
(`r fmt(grid_step(horm_pred))`). The increasing row has censored realisations,
so its crossings are compared as order statistics.

```{r}
#| label: fig-hormetic
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Every tenth realisation of the hormetic set, with both references and both NSECs and their intervals."
plot_nsec(horm_pred, horm)
```

@fig-hormetic shows the two crossings on most curves: an increasing one before
the peak at $x = 2$, and a decreasing one after it. Two features of the result
are absent from the monotone sets.

The realisation with control `r ctl(controls[1])` starts below the decreasing
reference, but it rises above the reference and falls through it at
`r fmt(horm_first_dec)`. That is a crossing in the direction sought, so `nsec()`
gives it that concentration, although its response first rises away from the
effect.

The `r n_horm_censored` realisations with the lowest controls peak below the
increasing reference. The highest of them peaks at
$2e^{-1/2} \times `r ctl(controls[n_horm_censored])` = `r fmt(peak * controls[n_horm_censored], 5)`$,
against `r ctl(r_inc)`. They never cross upward, so they are censored. They are
`r pct(n_horm_censored / n_real)` of the realisations, so the upper limit of the
increasing NSEC is reported as the highest concentration,
`r fmt(horm$conf.high[2])`, and the call warns. The warning suggests a wider
`x_range`, but a wider range would not resolve the censoring, because these
realisations decline beyond $x = 2$. The upper limit would be reported at the
new highest concentration. It records that more than 2.5 per cent of the
realisations show no increase past the reference anywhere in the tested range.

## The anchor argument

`anchor` names where the reference comes from when the realisations come from a
model average. A model average combines several fitted equations by weight, and
each of its realisations is drawn from one of those equations, its component.
`anchor` is reported as a column of the result.

`anchor = "model"` takes the reference from all the control realisations of
the curve, pooled across components, as in every example above.
Every realisation is then measured against one response level, which can be
drawn on a plot as in @fig-decreasing.

`anchor = "component"` measures the realisations of each component against the
`sig_val` quantile of that component's own control realisations. That is the
strict Bayesian model average, and the reference `bayesnec::nsec()` uses for a
model set, so it is the default for a `bayesmanecfit`; `"model"` is the default
otherwise. For a `bayesmanecfit` each component's quantile is taken over every
draw of its own fit, not only the draws kept in the average. For a fit that is
not a model average there is one component, so the two anchors give the same
values.

```{r}
#| label: anchor-single
dec_component <- nsec(dec_pred, anchor = "component")
dec_component[, c("direction", "estimate", "conf.low", "conf.high", "anchor")]
```

```{r}
#| label: anchor-single-check
#| echo: false
stopifnot(
  identical(dec_component$estimate, dec$estimate),
  identical(dec_component$conf.low, dec$conf.low),
  identical(dec_component$conf.high, dec$conf.high)
)
```

A model average is recognised from `meta$draw_model`, which names the component of each
realisation. The constructed set below assigns the realisations of the
decreasing set with controls up to the median to an equation `a`, and the rest
to an equation `b`.

```{r}
#| label: anchor-average
draw_model <- ifelse(controls <= median(controls), "a", "b")
avg_pred <- build_pred(
  decline,
  controls,
  seq(0, 10, length.out = 500),
  model_weights = c(table(draw_model)) / length(draw_model),
  draw_model = draw_model
)
avg_component <- nsec(avg_pred, anchor = "component")
avg_component[, c("direction", "estimate", "conf.low", "conf.high", "anchor")]
```

```{r}
#| label: anchor-average-values
#| echo: false
ref_by_component <- tapply(controls, draw_model, quantile, probs = 0.01)
n_by_component <- table(draw_model)
range_by_component <- tapply(controls, draw_model, range)
```

Under `"model"` every realisation is measured against `r ctl(r_dec)`. Under
`"component"` the `r n_by_component[["a"]]` realisations of `a`, with controls
from `r ctl(range_by_component[["a"]][1])` to `r ctl(range_by_component[["a"]][2])`, are
measured against `r ctl(ref_by_component[["a"]])`. The
`r n_by_component[["b"]]` realisations of `b`, with controls from
`r ctl(range_by_component[["b"]][1])` to `r ctl(range_by_component[["b"]][2])`, are
measured against `r ctl(ref_by_component[["b"]])`. Each is the 0.01 quantile of
that equation's own controls. Applying `nsec()` to the realisations of each
equation alone, and summarising their crossings together, gives the same NSEC as
`anchor = "component"`.

```{r}
#| label: anchor-average-component
component_nsec <- lapply(split(seq_along(controls), draw_model), function(rows) {
  one_equation <- build_pred(decline, controls[rows], seq(0, 10, length.out = 500))
  nsec(one_equation, draws = TRUE)$draws[[1]]$value.draw
})
model_nsec <- nsec(avg_pred, draws = TRUE)
rbind(
  model = unlist(model_nsec[1, c("estimate", "conf.low", "conf.high")]),
  component = quantile(unlist(component_nsec), probs, names = FALSE)
)
```

```{r}
#| label: anchor-average-component-check
#| echo: false
q_component <- quantile(unlist(component_nsec), probs, names = FALSE)
model_draws <- model_nsec$draws[[1]]$value.draw
stopifnot(
  identical(model_nsec$estimate, dec$estimate),
  identical(model_nsec$conf.low, dec$conf.low),
  identical(model_nsec$conf.high, dec$conf.high),
  isTRUE(all.equal(
    unlist(avg_component[1, c("estimate", "conf.low", "conf.high")]),
    q_component,
    check.attributes = FALSE
  )),
  # the component interval is narrower, and its upper limit lower
  diff(q_component[2:3]) < model_nsec$conf.high[1] - model_nsec$conf.low[1],
  q_component[3] < model_nsec$conf.high[1],
  # under "model" every realisation above the upper limit belongs to `b`,
  # whose own reference lies above the pooled one
  all(draw_model[model_draws > model_nsec$conf.high[1]] == "b"),
  ref_by_component[["b"]] > r_dec
)
```

Under `"component"` the NSEC is `r fmt(q_component[1])` (`r fmt(q_component[2])`
to `r fmt(q_component[3])`), against `r fmt(model_nsec$estimate[1])`
(`r fmt(model_nsec$conf.low[1])` to `r fmt(model_nsec$conf.high[1])`) under
`"model"`. Here the interval is narrower. The NSEC of each realisation decreases
when its equation's own reference lies above the pooled one, and increases when
it lies below. Which way the width changes depends on which realisations set the
limits under `"model"`. Here the realisations of `b` set the upper limit, because
they are measured against a reference well below their controls. Under
`"component"` they are measured against `r ctl(ref_by_component[["b"]])`, their
NSECs decrease, and the upper limit decreases with them. Where an equation whose
reference lies above the pooled one holds the lowest NSECs instead, its NSECs
decrease further and the interval widens.

`anchor = "control"`, a reference taken from a model fitted to the control
observations alone, was proposed and is not implemented. `nsec()` refuses it.

```{r}
#| label: anchor-control
#| error: true
nsec(dec_pred, anchor = "control")
```

## A fitted model

The same calculation applies to a fitted model. `drc::drm()` fits the
four-parameter log-logistic equation `LL.4()` to the root lengths of ryegrass
exposed to ferulic acid, `drc::ryegrass`. `toxval_predict()` draws parametric
bootstrap replicates of the curve,
`r formals(toxval:::toxval_predict.drc)$n_boot` by default (`n_boot`), and
`nsec()` is called on the result.

```{r}
#| label: drc-fit
#| eval: !expr has_drc
fit <- drc::drm(rootl ~ conc, data = drc::ryegrass, fct = drc::LL.4())
rye_pred <- toxval_predict(fit, seed = 42)
rye <- nsec(rye_pred)
show_nsec(rye)
```

```{r}
#| label: drc-check
#| echo: false
#| eval: !expr has_drc
rye_control <- rye_pred$curves[[1]][, 1]
# a replicate with no increasing crossing is either placed at `x_control` or
# censored (`Inf`); none has a crossing above the control concentration
rye_inc <- nsec(rye_pred, draws = TRUE)$draws[[2]]$value.draw
stopifnot(
  isTRUE(all.equal(
    rye$reference,
    unname(quantile(rye_control, c(0.01, 0.99)))
  )),
  isTRUE(all.equal(
    as.data.frame(nsec(fit, seed = 42)),
    as.data.frame(rye)
  )),
  length(rye_control) == formals(toxval:::toxval_predict.drc)$n_boot,
  !any(is.finite(rye_inc) & rye_inc > rye_pred$meta$x_control),
  isTRUE(all.equal(
    rye$ecnsec[1],
    quantile(1 - rye$reference[1] / rye_control, 0.5, names = FALSE)
  ))
)
# the lowest two concentrations tested, against which the figure is read
rye_tested <- sort(unique(drc::ryegrass$conc[drc::ryegrass$conc > 0]))[1:2]
stopifnot(
  rye$conf.low[1] < rye_tested[1],
  rye_tested[1] < rye$estimate[1],
  rye$conf.high[1] < rye_tested[2]
)
```

The decreasing reference is `r if_drc(fmt(rye$reference[1]))`, the 0.01
quantile of the `r if_drc(length(rye_control))` bootstrap controls, whose median
is `r if_drc(fmt(rye$control[1]))`. The NSEC is
`r if_drc(fmt(rye$estimate[1]))` (`r if_drc(fmt(rye$conf.low[1]))` to
`r if_drc(fmt(rye$conf.high[1]))`), and the reference lies
`r if_drc(pct(rye$ecnsec[1]))` below the control at the median. `nsec(fit,
seed = 42)` gives the same result in one call. No replicate crosses the
increasing reference, so the increasing row is `NA`.

```{r}
#| label: fig-ryegrass-nsec
#| echo: false
#| eval: !expr has_drc
#| fig-cap: "The `LL.4()` fit to `drc::ryegrass`: root lengths (grey points), the curve at the parameter estimates (black line) and the 95 per cent band of the bootstrap replicates (grey band), on a log concentration axis with the controls drawn at the tick labelled 0. Dashed lines are the two references; the vermillion line and band are the decreasing NSEC and its 95 per cent interval, from `nsec(rye_pred)` and identically from `nsec(fit, seed = 42)`. The increasing NSEC is `NA` and is not drawn."
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-height: 4.2
rye_data <- drc::ryegrass
# A log axis cannot show the control at 0, so the controls are drawn at
# `x_zero`, left of the lowest concentration tested, as drc's own plot method
# does; the curve and band start clear of that position.
x_zero <- 0.4
rye_x <- ifelse(rye_data$conc == 0, x_zero, rye_data$conc)
on_axis <- rye_pred$x_vec >= 0.6
x_log <- exp(seq(log(0.6), log(30), length.out = 300))
band <- apply(rye_pred$curves[[1]][, on_axis], 2, quantile, c(0.025, 0.975))
stopifnot(max(band[2, ]) < rye$reference[2])
nsec_col <- "#D55E00"
op <- par(mar = c(4, 4, 1, 1))
plot(rye_x, rye_data$rootl, log = "x", type = "n", xaxt = "n", las = 1,
     bty = "l", xlab = "Concentration", ylab = "Root length")
axis(1, at = c(x_zero, sort(unique(rye_data$conc))[-1]),
     labels = sort(unique(rye_data$conc)))
polygon(c(rye_pred$x_vec[on_axis], rev(rye_pred$x_vec[on_axis])),
        c(band[1, ], rev(band[2, ])), col = "grey85", border = NA)
rect(rye$conf.low[1], par("usr")[3], rye$conf.high[1], par("usr")[4],
     col = adjustcolor(nsec_col, 0.2), border = NA)
points(rye_x, rye_data$rootl, pch = 19, col = "grey50")
lines(x_log, predict(fit, newdata = data.frame(conc = x_log)), lwd = 2)
abline(h = rye$reference, lty = 2, col = "grey20")
text(30, rye$reference, paste(rye$direction, "reference"), adj = c(1, -0.4),
     col = "grey20", cex = 0.8)
abline(v = rye$estimate[1], col = nsec_col, lwd = 2)
legend("bottomleft", bty = "n", cex = 0.85,
       legend = c("decreasing NSEC", "95% interval", "bootstrap 95% band"),
       col = c(nsec_col, adjustcolor(nsec_col, 0.2), "grey85"),
       lty = 1, lwd = c(2, 10, 10))
par(op)
```

In @fig-ryegrass-nsec the NSEC lies between the two lowest concentrations
tested, `r if_drc(rye_tested[1])` and `r if_drc(rye_tested[2])`, and the lower
limit of its interval lies below `r if_drc(rye_tested[1])`. The NSEC is located
on the bootstrap curves rather than at a tested concentration, so it can fall
between or below the concentrations tested. The increasing reference lies above
the band of replicates at every concentration drawn.

## Provenance

The realisations in every example except the last are constructed, with no
random element. The `drc` example draws its bootstrap replicates with
`seed = 42`, passed to `toxval_predict()`, and uses `drc::ryegrass` as
distributed with `drc`. Every grid has 500 points, the default `resolution`, and
every hand-computed NSEC is checked against `nsec()` to within one grid step.

```{r}
#| label: provenance
#| echo: false
versions <- c(
  R = paste(R.version$major, R.version$minor, sep = "."),
  toxval = as.character(utils::packageVersion("toxval"))
)
if (has_drc) {
  versions["drc"] <- as.character(utils::packageVersion("drc"))
}
versions
```
